<text:style bold="true">Main Purpose</text:style>

<image:base64 col="0" width="84" wrap="none"></image:base64>

TTPaint is a<text:style bold="true"> drawing program</text:style>. It is not a photo editor: it is made to create icons,
diagrams and schemes, didactic images (pictures that explain something) and, why
not, to have fun drawing.

It has both basic<text:style bold="true"> technical drawing</text:style> capabilities and<text:style bold="true"> creative drawing</text:style> ones. For
technical drawing there are lines, polygons, circles and arcs, parallel copies,
fillets and chamfers, mirror and array copies, reference lines and points, quotes
(dimensions) and geometric constraints: the drawing keeps its rules when something
is moved. For creative drawing there are pens, markers, an airbrush, fills with
colours, gradients, hatching and materials, soft edges, layers with filters, and
raster tools to work on the pictures that are pasted in the drawing.

It is meant to be<text:style bold="true"> easy to use and intuitive</text:style>: the tools are grouped in panels at the
top of the window, every object has its properties at the right, the most frequent
choices (thickness, line style, colours) are in the bar at the bottom, and a click
with the right mouse button on an object offers the operations that make sense for
it.

The main window:

- The panels at the top hold the tools: Geometric Tools, Artistic Tools, Raster
  Tools, Actions, Constraints, Colors (or Materials), Quotes, References, Operators
  and SVG Snippets.
- The drawing area is at the left; the zoom slider is at the bottom right (Ctrl +
  mouse wheel zooms too).
- At the right there are the layers, the objects of the drawing and the Properties
  of what is selected.
- The bar at the bottom shows the thickness and the style of the line, the primary
  and the secondary colours, the transparency of the pasted pictures, the tolerance
  and the size of the image.

The next topics describe each of these parts.
